I am 60 this year, and I have farmed in Quzhou for 40 years. I have only 15 mu, so I cannot spread myself too thin, and with only 2 people in the household and some off-farm work, labor matters as much as yield. I will keep the land in the pattern I trust most: 10 mu in winter wheat followed by summer maize, and 5 mu in cotton. Wheat-maize gives me stable grain income and spreads risk; cotton can still make money, but it needs more hand labor, so I will not expand it. I have well water, so I am not fully dependent on rain, but pumping costs money, so I will irrigate at the key stages rather than too often.

For the 2026 season, the winter wheat is already in the field because it was planted in October 2025. On wheat, I will stay with a medium-high input plan because the stand looks worth supporting. I will topdress mainly at jointing and watch leaf color, then give 3 irrigations if the weather stays normal: jointing, heading, and grain filling if the soil turns dry. After wheat harvest in June 2026, I will not waste time with heavy tillage before maize. The turnaround is too tight. I will use a simple harvest-then-plant approach with one shallow pass or direct seeding if the machine is available. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and keep fertilizer moderate, because maize responds well here but I do not want to overspend after the wheat season. On cotton, I will keep only 5 mu because picking takes time and my household labor is limited. I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, 2 irrigations, and I will control weeds and bollworm on time. I am not chasing the highest possible yield; I am protecting stable output and keeping cash flow manageable.
